question.text: If the integral <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>∫</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>-</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></math><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></math> (where, <math><mi>C</mi></math> is the constant of integration) and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi>e</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo></math> then the number of natural numbers less than <math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to (where,  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="[" close="]" separators="|"><mo>·</mo></mfenced></math> is the greatest integer function)

solution.text:
